title: The Marathas and the 18th Century Struggle for Power

questions.question: Shivaji was born in 1630 at which fort?
questions.rationale: Shivaji was born at Shivneri fort to Shahji Bhosle and Jijabai; he captured his first fort, Torna, in 1646 and made Raigad his capital.

questions.question: The Treaty of Purandar (1665), by which Shivaji ceded 23 forts, was signed with:
questions.rationale: Jai Singh I's Mughal campaign forced the Treaty of Purandar in 1665; Shivaji's subsequent visit to Agra ended in his famous escape.

questions.question: Shivaji's coronation as Chhatrapati at Raigad was performed by:
questions.rationale: Gaga Bhatt of Varanasi officiated at the coronation of 6 June 1674, giving ritual legitimacy and the title Haindava Dharmodharak.

questions.question: 'Chauth' and 'sardeshmukhi' respectively claimed:
options: One-fourth and an additional one-tenth of revenue
A fixed tribute and military service
Half the produce and free labour
questions.rationale: Chauth was one-fourth of a territory's revenue in exchange for protection; sardeshmukhi was an extra one-tenth claimed as an overlord's hereditary due — 35% together.

questions.question: Which Peshwa secured sanads from Delhi granting Maratha claims over the six Deccan provinces?
questions.rationale: Balaji Vishwanath marched to Delhi in 1719 to support the Sayyid brothers and returned with sanads legalising chauth and sardeshmukhi across the Deccan.

questions.question: Baji Rao I's celebrated victory over the Nizam in 1728 was at:
questions.rationale: Baji Rao I outmanoeuvred the Nizam at Palkhed in 1728 and again at Bhopal in 1737; he died in 1740 without losing a battle.

questions.question: In the Third Battle of Panipat (14 January 1761), the Maratha commander was:
questions.rationale: Sadashivrao Bhau led the Marathas against Ahmad Shah Abdali; Vishwasrao and Bhau himself died in the defeat.

questions.question: The Maratha admiral who dominated the Konkan coast from Kolaba was:
questions.rationale: Kanhoji Angre, Sarkhel of Kolaba (1698-1729), made Maratha sea power supreme on the western coast for three decades.

questions.question: At the Battle of Wandiwash (1760), Eyre Coote defeated:
questions.rationale: Wandiwash on 22 January 1760 ended the third Carnatic war: Coote defeated the Comte de Lally, and by the Peace of Paris (1763) France kept only unfortified trading posts.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT listed as a reason for English success against Indian powers?
options: A single united Indian confederacy opposing them
questions.rationale: Indian powers fought separately — Marathas, Mysore, and the Nizam never made common cause — which, with sea power, finance, and a disciplined sepoy army, secured English victory.
